title: Affine etale pairs test absolute quasi-separatedness
statement: Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Absolute quasi-separatedness is the notion of [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated], equivalently quasi-compactness on scheme tests of the absolute diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$. Then $X$ is absolutely quasi-separated if and only if, for every pair of affine schemes $U,V$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and representable etale morphisms $U\to X$ and $V\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], the scheme $U\times_XV$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. No quasi-compactness, separation or Noetherian assumption on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1): only affine open pieces of an etale atlas are used. This etale-pair variant is also explicitly used at the start of decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6.

proof.text: If $X$ is absolutely quasi-separated, the affine-test definition [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$) applies to every pair in the question, since etale maps are in particular maps to $X$. Their fibre product is a scheme: the representable diagonal of [def-trf-algebraic-space] represents $h_U\times_Xh_V$ by the scheme $X\times_{X\times X}(U\times_{\mathbf Z}V)$, a pair of sections with equal image in $X$ being the same as a section of $X$ together with a section of $U\times V$ with the same image in $X\times X$. The definition asserts quasi-compactness of its point space. For a scheme $T$ the identity is a representable surjective etale atlas of $h_T$, and $|\mathrm{id}|:|T|\to|h_T|$ is bijective: a map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ with image $t$ has the class of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$, and two residue-field points with a common extension have the same image. By the independence of the atlas in [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], the point space of $h_T$ is therefore the Zariski space of $T$. So the quasi-compactness asserted by the definition is precisely the required quasi-compactness of the scheme $U\times_XV$.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1), restricted to affine opens of an etale atlas; also decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated), first paragraph.

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated condition on affine etale pairs. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:W\to X$ with $W=\coprod_i U_i$ and each $U_i$ affine, by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Each component is an open subscheme of $W$. The inclusion $h_{U_i}\to h_W$ is representable etale: for a scheme $T$ and $h_T\to h_W$ its pullback is represented by $U_i\times_WT\to T$, an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Composition in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], together with its equivalence of chartwise and representable etale for scheme sources, makes $p_i:U_i\to X$ representable etale. Consequently $R_{ij}=U_i\times_XU_j$ is a scheme and is quasi-compact by the hypothesis, for every $i,j$.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1), restricted to affine opens of an etale atlas; also decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated), first paragraph.

proof.text: All products in the rest of the proof are over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Set $B=W\times W$ and $Y=X\times X$. Factor $p\times p$ as $W\times W\to X\times W\to X\times X$. These arrows are base changes of $p$ along the respective projections, hence representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Their composite $q:B\to Y$ is a surjective etale covering by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The diagonal $\Delta_X$ is representable by [def-trf-algebraic-space], so its pullback $j:R\to B$ has scheme source. The fibre-product universal property identifies $R=X\times_YB$ with $W\times_XW$, and $j$ with its two projections into $W$.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1), restricted to affine opens of an etale atlas; also decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated), first paragraph.

proof.text: For each $i,j$, let $Q_{ij}=U_i\times U_j$. Its map to $B$ factors as $U_i\times U_j\to W\times U_j\to W\times W$, two base changes of open inclusions, so it is an open inclusion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Its image is $\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}(U_i)\cap\operatorname{pr}_2^{-1}(U_j)$: a map to $B$ factors through it exactly when both projections factor through the indicated opens, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. These images cover $B$ because the $U_i$ cover $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Q_{ij}$ is affine, with ring $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\Gamma(U_j,\mathcal O)$. The same universal property identifies $j^{-1}(Q_{ij})=R\times_BQ_{ij}$ with $U_i\times_XU_j=R_{ij}$, compatibly with its map to $Q_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1), restricted to affine opens of an etale atlas; also decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated), first paragraph.

proof.text: Each $Q_{ij}$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $R_{ij}$ is quasi-compact by step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $R_{ij}\to Q_{ij}$ a quasi-compact scheme morphism. These are the restrictions of $j$ to the open cover just constructed. Thus [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] makes $j:R\to B$ quasi-compact. No finiteness of the cover and no quasi-separatedness of $W$ or $R$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1), restricted to affine opens of an etale atlas; also decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated), first paragraph.

proof.text: The descent node [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] tests quasi-compactness of a morphism on quasi-compact algebraic spaces; we first check that $j$ passes this test. Let $Z$ be a quasi-compact space with $Z\to B$, and $T\to Z$ a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme. The scheme $R\times_BT$ is quasi-compact over $T$ by the base-change clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], hence quasi-compact by its clause (2). Transitivity of fibre products identifies $R\times_BT$ with $(R\times_BZ)\times_ZT$, so by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] it maps representably, surjectively and etale onto $R\times_BZ$. Thus $R\times_BZ$ is a quasi-compact space and $j$ is quasi-compact in that sense. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] to $\Delta_X:X\to Y$ and the singleton covering $\{q:B\to Y\}$. It is jointly surjective by step 3; each scheme test of $q$ is etale and hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], exactly the descent hypotheses. Its pullback of $\Delta_X$ is $j$, so $\Delta_X$ is quasi-compact on quasi-compact space tests. A quasi-compact scheme is such a test, by its identity atlas and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] for affine ones, so $\Delta_X$ is quasi-compact in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], whose representable-morphism equivalence now gives quasi-compactness on every scheme test of $\Delta_X$.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), proof of (3) implies (1), restricted to affine opens of an etale atlas; also decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated), first paragraph.

proof.text: It remains to verify the affine-test definition [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated] itself, without using the remark on the diagonal recorded there. Let $U,V$ be affine schemes with arbitrary maps $h_U\to X$, $h_V\to X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] over $\mathbf Z$, $U\times V$ is affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. As in step 1, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $h_U\times_Xh_V$ with the scheme $P=X\times_Y(U\times V)$, the base change of $\Delta_X$ along $U\times V\to Y$. By step 6, $P\to U\times V$ is a quasi-compact morphism of schemes; its target is quasi-compact, so $P$ is quasi-compact by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its point space is its Zariski space by step 1, using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Hence $X$ is absolutely quasi-separated. Together with step 1 this proves the desired equivalence. Steps 1 to 7 also prove the equivalence with quasi-compactness of the absolute diagonal on scheme tests mentioned in the statement. All atlas products and the diagonal were absolute products over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.
